policy_extraction.implementation_notes: The EU AI Pact is a non-binding initiative promoted by the European Commission and its AI Office to help stakeholders prepare during the EU AI Act transitional period (following the AI Act's entry into force on 2024-08-01). It comprises two pillars: Pillar I (an open stakeholder network for webinars and best-practice sharing) and Pillar II (voluntary company pledges, or 'declarations of engagement', launched with first signatories on 2024-09-25 and signed by over 230 companies). Core pledges cover adopting an AI governance strategy, identifying and mapping likely high-risk AI systems, and promoting staff AI literacy; additional optional pledges cover human oversight, risk mitigation, and transparency for AI-generated content such as deepfakes. Pledges carry no legal obligations or sanctions.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document's dominant frame is innovation_enablement because the AI Pact is justified primarily as a voluntary, collaborative mechanism to help organisations prepare smoothly for AI Act compliance, foster organisational AI uptake, share best practices, and build trust in trustworthy AI deployment. It edges out fundamental_rights and consumer_public_safety, which appear mainly as concise background objectives in the Big Picture section ('ensuring safety and fundamental rights') and in references to risk mitigation and deep-fake transparency rather than as the central rationale of the Pact itself. A minor nod to economic_competitiveness appears in the reference to boosting research and industrial capacity.
